instruction: CLI-only OpenSCAD quantified CAD optimization task. Work from /home/user/Desktop/starter.scad, /home/user/Desktop/baseline.stl, and /home/user/Desktop/constraints.json. Use OpenSCAD command-line modeling and export, not a GUI. Edit /home/user/Desktop/starter.scad or create a derived OpenSCAD source file, then export the final geometry as STL. This is a continuous-score optimization task, not a request to match one hidden answer. Case: long lightweight cable-tray bridge. Objective: Maximize useful span-height stiffness proxy per material volume for a long cable-tray bridge. Hard constraints: keep the final STL within envelope [130.0, 38.0, 45.0] mm, keep each bounding-box span at least [124.0, 32.0, 36.0] mm, keep material volume between 52000.0 and 98000.0 mm^3, and keep the required base/contact footprint usable. Optimize for this evaluator metric after hard constraints are checked: (bbox_x_mm * bbox_z_mm) / volume_mm3; longer and deeper bridge geometry with less material receives a higher score. Required outputs: /home/user/Desktop/optimized.stl and /home/user/Desktop/design_summary.json. The benchmark evaluates the real exported STL geometry. Do not read or copy ground_truth, do not edit eval.py, and do not fabricate metric files without producing a valid STL.
